title: Living style guide page
when: The user wants one page that shows the design system: colors, type, spacing, buttons, forms and components with their states.
prompt:
Goal: styleguide.html that renders every token and component from the real stylesheet, so it stays true as the CSS changes.
Steps:
1. Link the same tokens.css and style.css the site uses; add only a small styleguide.css for the page frame.
2. Give each family an h2 section: Colors, Typography, Spacing, Radius and elevation, Buttons, Forms, Components, Motion.
3. Colors: a swatch per token with name, hex, and its text pair with the contrast ratio; swatch labels in a passing color.
4. Typography: each scale step as a real sentence with the token name; spacing as bars of each step width.
5. Components in every state side by side (default, hover via an .is-hover class, focus, disabled, error), with escaped markup in pre and code.
6. Add a contents nav of anchor links and one usage rule per section (One primary button per view).
Quality bar:
- Uses the real classes, never copies of styles.
- Every state visible without interaction.
- The page passes the same checks as the site.
Pitfalls:
- Hard coded swatch colors that drift from the tokens.
- Unescaped samples that render instead of showing code.
- A guide nobody can find; link it from the README.
Verify:
- [ ] styleguide.html links the site CSS.
- [ ] Each token family has a section.
- [ ] Component states are shown.
- [ ] Code samples are escaped.
Output: styleguide.html and styleguide.css next to the site files.

examples.input: make a style guide page for our components
examples.output: styleguide.html with color swatches and ratios, type scale, button states, form states, contents nav
